name: Synspective StriX

overview.value: Synspective is a Japanese company that builds and operates small synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites. It provides SAR data and analytics solutions.

base.reason: press-wire release (not a registry-recognized aggregator or direct-record host), single reference; landed crossfeed flag_refresh candidate (item snr 4 in items.json). Page states "Electron has flawlessly deployed all 13 StriX satellites to orbit with 100% mission success" (weekly registry maintenance 2026-10-05).

orbit.value: Sun Synchronous Orbit at 500 km altitude

base.reason: eoPortal mission page (ESA-run aggregator); page states Staring Spotlight mode enables 'ultra-high-resolution imaging down to ~0.25 m azimuth resolution in advanced configurations' (registry v2 EO spec backfill, cite-facts-only per terms)
eoPortal mission page (ESA-run aggregator); page states 'StriX uses X-band for high-resolution urban monitoring and infrastructure assessment' (registry v2 EO spec backfill)

notes: Company newsroom announced first imagery from its seventh satellite (2026-07 fetch); on-orbit total not stated as a figure. eoPortal (page last updated Jun 16, 2026) states Stripmap ground range resolution 'approximately 3.6 m' over a 'typical swath width of 10-30 km' (range kept in the mode name, not reduced to one number), Sliding Spotlight 'down to approximately 0.46 m' over 'around 10 km', Staring Spotlight '~0.25 m azimuth resolution'. EO backfill attempt (2026-08-20): checked eoPortal and synspective.com/satellite/strix-constellation/ for a constellation-level swath_km and a revisit figure. eoPortal states swath only per mode (Stripmap 10-30 km, Sliding/Staring Spotlight ~10 km), already carried in imaging_modes, with no single constellation-wide figure to backfill. Synspective's own constellation page states only the design aim to 'observe the same location under the same conditions daily' with no numeric revisit figure (vague aspirational language, not coerced into a number per house rule). swath_km and revisit left absent/null. Weekly maintenance 2026-09-03: sats_launched_total and latest_launch_date refreshed to 11 / 2026-09-02 via Launch Library's naming of Rocket Lab's 2026-09-02 mission ("Owl Around The World (StriX Launch 11)"). A crossfeed candidate for the same field/value from Rocket Lab's own GlobeNewswire mission-success release was rejected: the release states only "the latest StriX satellite" with no cumulative number, so it does not itself support the value 11 per the no-invented-figures rule. sats_active_claimed left at 10 (still sourced to the 10th-launch release): no source yet states the StriX-11 satellite has reached active/operational status. Weekly maintenance 2026-09-21: sats_launched_total and latest_launch_date refreshed to 12 / 2026-09-19 via Launch Library's naming of Rocket Lab's 2026-09-19 mission ("Owl By The Dozen (StriX Launch 12)"), landing a crossfeed flag_refresh candidate for the same field/value from Rocket Lab's own GlobeNewswire mission-success release, which this time does state the cumulative figure directly ("delivered the 12th StriX satellite"). sats_active_claimed still left at 10: no source yet states StriX-11 or StriX-12 have reached active/operational status. Weekly maintenance 2026-10-05: sats_launched_total and latest_launch_date refreshed to 13 / 2026-09-26 landing a crossfeed flag_refresh candidate from Rocket Lab's GlobeNewswire release for its 97th Electron mission, which states "Electron has flawlessly deployed all 13 StriX satellites to orbit with 100% mission success." A separate crossfeed candidate proposing sats_planned = 47 (from Rocket Lab's 2026-09-30 release on a new 20-launch Electron contract) was rejected, not landed: the release states the deal "brings the total number of Electron missions for Synspective to 47", a cumulative Electron-launch-contract count, not a stated total of planned StriX satellites; the two are not the same metric (Electron has carried a mix of single/multi-satellite StriX missions) and the release names no fleet-size target. sats_planned (30, first-party, as_of 2026-07-05) is left unchanged.
